translated_text: My dearest, sweet Zabalein, I can't even tell you how happy your lovely gifts made me, and your letter. I was already over the miscarriage, just a little tired from the emotional strain. But after your letter, I think I've really changed. It was someone who shook me up and told me to pull myself together a little. Today I'm feeling very cheerful again (although actually, a 25th birthday shouldn't be a reason to be, it just reminds you how old you are and I've almost forgotten everything). But I think it's more a feeling of joy stemming from a certain excitement, having come away with relatively little damage. You resist thinking back on it with all your might because you really need that little bit of good cheer. Father is doing very, very well today; he's even allowed to go out a little tomorrow. It was particularly complicated for him because his appendix was fused to his main intestine. Mother had a bad cold and is almost completely recovered. But what proves I'm the old Rob again is that on Sunday I was driving around with some Chrysler obstacles. I just want to be with you, my dear, so you could see it for yourself. We were unfortunately in Freudenstadt and it was very nice. We've had a lot of snow for the last two days and I'll take advantage of the opportunity if possible. It won't be long now, because in 10 days I'll probably be... I have to travel again, which is awful. But this time I'm quite happy to go, although I don't know why, and a lot of work awaits me. In any case, I'm reacting with a certain optimism, the realization that there aren't only material things that could shake this foundation. At least for the moment. It's not always good to be like this. But I can't and won't change. When I'm sad, I'm really sad, and when I'm happy, it's usually exuberant and different; either I'm not working at all or I'm working hard. You don't have to notice this mood outwardly, it's still there. On my birthday, we were all alone at home and had a very nice chat. I was quite pleased that no one came, and so I went to bed early for the first time in a long time. I don't quite understand his fear of the Abitur (university entrance exam). You've worked quite well so far. A little bit of courage and a dash of cheekiness. Then you'll be fine. You're capable of both, so you'll manage. You mustn't let a certain amount of exam anxiety get the better of you. Let it be, it's usually much easier than you think. And if you're already working like this... Besides, I think it's important to be so consistent. In, failing. My dear, your high school diploma won't lift the bliss of a house. You can certainly help Laci just as much, if not more, without it, by being able to do it even earlier. Incidentally, it's at least as rare in England as it is at school in Paris. Or don't you think so? Zabalein, my dear, let me kiss you many times from your loving Rob.
